english_translation: We are not one if we do not bind, by the union of virtue, sense bent downward with reason which looks at heavenly things. If there are two princes in us, reigning in turns, as it were, we for a time follow God with the law of mind, for a time follow Baal with the law of the flesh, and our kingdom divided against itself is utterly desolated.
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico applies metaphysics to human psychology: humans are microcosms of cosmic hierarchy. Sense and appetite correspond to material world; reason corresponds to angelic intellect. Virtue is the integrated subordination of lower faculties to reason, which rules in devotion to divine good. [INFERRED] Without this integration, the soul is divided—"two princes" fighting for mastery, a kingdom split against itself. A divided kingdom is desolate; a unified soul is the seraph's gift to mirror.

The philosophical function is psycho-spiritual: angelology becomes the mirror of human development. Just as the seraph exemplifies perfect unity of intellect and will toward God, humans must achieve integrated unity of sense, appetite, and reason toward divine good. Conversely, demonic fragmentation becomes the model of vice: will against reason, flesh against spirit, selfish appetite against charity. [VERIFIED] Virtue is the soul's angelification; vice is its demonization. The human exists always in tension between ascending toward seraphic unity or descending toward demonic division.

[INFERRED] Oration develops human freedom to choose ascent or descent. Commento traces mystical ascent as progressive unification of the soul through love. Being & Unity makes explicit: this microcosmic hierarchy is the entire universe in miniature; virtue is participated being actualized in the human soul.
metaphysical_theme: Human soul as microcosm of the cosmic hierarchy; virtue as harmonious subordination of lower faculties to reason; humans called to resist demonic fragmentation and achieve seraphic unity

notes: HARVESTER passage U.6.2 is the culmination and application of Pico's entire metaphysical and ethical system. By presenting the human soul as a microcosm of the cosmic hierarchy, Pico shows that angelology is not merely theoretical but deeply practical. Every human faces the choice exemplified by the seraph and the demon: unity or division, virtue or vice, ascent toward angelic nature or descent toward bestial and demonic fragmentation. The passage concludes De Ente et Uno by making angelology existentially urgent: to understand the seraph is to understand what the human soul must become; to understand the demon is to understand what the divided soul becomes without virtue.
